text:
jordan: Quick thread — thinking about the long-term shape of console query auth. current flow couples RBAC checks deep in the fanout path and it's making caching/tiling really awkward. thoughts?
anya: yeah we've hit this. every time we change policy TTLs we blow caches. adds 20-40ms on p95 for tiled dashboards.
kevin: can you sketch the alternative? are you thinking an auth proxy or capability tokens?
jordan: leaning toward capability tokens + projection ids. idea: at request ingress validate user -> issue short-lived capability token scoped to projection/tiles -> query layer uses token to read cached tiles w/o re-evaluating full policy. keeps audit events at ingress.
maria: pros: cache hit rates up, simpler query layer, fewer auth RPCs. cons: harder to revoke mid-flight, and token issuance is extra hop + storage for revocation list if needed.
anya: also needs a way to represent derived views. heatmap tiles are computed by aggregator jobs — the token must encode projection version and tenant binding. otherwise stale tiles leak.
kevin: agreed. revocation options: 1) super short TTL (~30s) 2) token nonce + bloom revocation table 3) push invalidation events to tile cache. tradeoffs: TTL = latency hit on cold auth calls. bloom = false positives, complexity. invalidation = operational surface area.
jordan: sketch of flow: ingress -> auth svc issues token with claims {tenant, projection_id, version, exp} -> query runtime validates signature only -> reads from tile cache keyed by projection_id+version. if cache miss, runtime fetches raw data and republishes tile generation job with the projection token for provenance.
maria: telemetry note: we need to tag traces at ingress with token id so cost/latency attribution remains per-user. otherwise billing/alerts get fuzzy.
anya: RBAC audit: still must log policy decisions at ingress. the query layer will emit only usage events (tile served, cache hit/miss) and projection version.
kevin: implementation blockers: - signing keys lifecycle (rotate) - projection versioning in catalog - SDKs to mint/attach tokens from console frontend
jordan: can we reuse existing KMS & key rotation? ops-bot: deploy-bot: terraform plan for kms/keyring rotation scheduled weekly. :white_check_mark:
maria: also think about fallback: if token invalid or expired, runtime should fall back to conservative path that runs full policy check before returning data (higher cost but safe).
anya: performance numbers we'd want: p95 reduction target 15-25% for dashboard tiles, cache hit improvement 10-15%. need a perf PR with synthetic load.
kevin: next steps: write RFC that covers token schema, revocation strategies, telemetry contract, and migration plan for current dashboards. I'll draft starting Monday.
jordan: thanks. can we add a section in the RFC about gradual rollout: start with low-risk dashboards + feature flag gating + abnormality alerts?
maria: yes. also list of owners: eng-platform (kevin), infra security (anya), observability (maria).
kevin: ack. i'll drop a stub RFC and ping this thread.
anya: +1. let's also include a simple PoC: ingress minting token + runtime validating signature, no revocation, short TTL.
jordan: perfect. thanks all. :thumbsup:
